text:
maria: quick heads-up from the onboarding smoke tests: when many users import docs in parallel the client-side SDK window opens aggressively, server issues 429s, the clients respect Retry-After but retry both pages together and we end up with duplicate requests + cost spikes. anyone seen this pattern?
ravi: yep. replicates locally if you run 8 parallel import workers. server logs show short-lived bursts then a steady stream of retries.
tj: do we have an example of the headers coming back? curious whether it's Retry-After only or if we can add something more helpful.
maria: sample trace: 
```
POST /v1/embeds/batch 310ms
<- 429 Retry-After: 1
<- X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
<- body: {"code":"rate_limit","detail":"burst"}
```
maria: behavior: client waits 1s, retries both batches, server accepts one and 429s the other, client requeues and repeats.
sarah: two obvious failure modes: (A) SDK allows too many in-flight requests per logical session; (B) app-level workers independently read the same remaining tokens causing oversubscribe.
lee: noticed also that JS SDK's jitter implementation sometimes produces near-zero jitter in worker threads (seed reuse). Go looks less affected because of goroutine scheduler randomness. parity bug.
ravi: mitigation plan: introduce conservative slow-start defaults + a per-session max-inflight setting in SDKs (config: maxInFlightPerSession). Default to 4 for onboarding flows.
tj: server-side help: add an advisory header like X-Queue-Position or X-Shed-Advice so clients can stagger retries instead of hammering together. Also consider returning a session-level multiplier (X-Backoff-Factor) so clients converge.
sarah: I'll prototype X-Queue-Pos and X-Backoff-Factor in the rate limiter. documentation will recommend a client pacing algo: slow-start (1 in-flight), double every success until max, on 429 multiply backoff by server factor and apply jitter.
maria: sampleapp change: put a tiny leaky-bucket in front of the SDK calls for onboarding flows. pseudo: 
```
// acquire or wait
if (!bucket.tryAcquire()) { await sleep(random(50,200)); continue; }
await sdk.embed(batch)
```
This prevents the initial synchronized ramp.
lee: will open a PR to fix the jitter seed in JS SDK and add a small entropy check that logs a warning if jitter variance < threshold.
ravi: I'll add maxInFlightPerSession to go-sdk + js-sdk and wire up an env override for sampleapps. also add an e2e test that simulates 10 parallel imports and asserts we don't get >2x duplicate work.
tj: short-term: sampleapp maintainers, can you flip onboarding to use the leaky-bucket helper and set maxInFlightPerSession=4? will reduce incident noise.
ci-bot: New issue created: INF-4333 "onboard window throttling & SDK slow-starts" assigned to @ravi @sarah @lee :white_check_mark:
maria: also propose SDK telemetry: emit metric when >3 retries within 30s for same session and tag "onboarding". that way we can alert on churn and surface to runtime dashboard.
sarah: agreed. add to INF-4333. I'll draft a short doc block with the recommended pacing algorithm and a tiny sampleapp walkthrough.
ravi: timeline? i can get SDK flags + tests in 1 sprint. server header + doc in parallel.
maria: perfect. i'll coordinate sampleapp PRs and add a short howto for mobile clients. thanks all. :thumbsup:
